notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). Source: 2024 annual report on Form 20-F (accession 0001140361-25-018954, filed May 14, 2025), read on EDGAR; financial statements are in thousands of Mexican pesos (IFRS), recorded here in billions of MXN with no FX conversion. Cash values match the SEC XBRL (ifrs-full) facts. OWNERSHIP (as of March 31, 2025, percentages of the 60,740 million B Shares outstanding, per footnote 1; the 20-F does not say whether treasury shares are excluded): the 20-F lists three holders above 5%, all linked to the Slim Family: the Family Trust 29.2%, Control Empresarial de Capitales 17.9%, and Carlos Slim Helú 8.6%. They are recorded as three non-overlapping figures: Carlos Slim's own 8.6% as the leader, the Family Trust as the family figure, and Control Empresarial de Capitales as a holder. The 20-F says family members' direct shares are 'in addition to shares held by the Family Trust', and Control Empresarial holds its shares through its own subsidiaries. The 20-F's 22.7% for direct holdings of all Slim Family members is NOT recorded because it includes Carlos Slim's 8.6% (overlap); the other family members' direct holdings (including directors Carlos Slim Domit, 3.8%, and Patrick Slim Domit, 2.0%) therefore do not appear. No all-inclusive family total is stated, and the figures were not summed. pctVoting is null because there is a single series with one vote per share. Relation 'founder' follows data.js; the 20-F does not use the word. DIVIDENDS: the cash-flow line 'Dividends paid' (Ps.31,007,121 thousand) does not separate dividends to non-controlling interests; the statement of changes in equity shows 2024 dividends declared of Ps.29,482,507 thousand to owners of the parent and Ps.2,021,059 thousand to non-controlling interests, and the MD&A says 'We paid Ps.31.0 billion in dividends in 2024'. No figure for dividends paid to the company's own shareholders alone is stated (the equity note gives only the Ps.0.48-per-share dividend approved April 29, 2024), so the cash line is used and labelled as total; it likely includes dividends paid to minority shareholders of subsidiaries. Nothing was subtracted. BUYBACKS: the cash-flow line (Ps.22,746,633 thousand); the equity statement shows Ps.22,740,293 thousand, and the MD&A says 'We spent Ps.22.7 billion repurchasing our own shares in the open market in 2024'. STOCK COMP: null; the 20-F discloses no share-based compensation expense or employee share plan. GEOGRAPHY: external revenues (after removing Ps.37,051,975 thousand of intersegment revenues) by the company's reportable segments; they sum to consolidated total revenues.

footprint.notes: Subscribers come from the 20-F's RGU table by reportable segment (thousands). Mexico, Brazil, Colombia and Argentina are single-country segments and appear as country rows; multi-country segments are regions whose country lists are the 20-F's own segment definitions. Employees are reported only for Mexico and four broad regions (South America, Central America, Caribbean, Europe), which the filing does not define by country, so those region rows carry no country list. Because each quote covers one table row, each country or region appears once per metric (wireless RGUs, fixed RGUs, employees); merge rows by iso2/name when displaying. Wireless and fixed RGUs should not be summed into customers (one customer can hold several RGUs). No U.S. state data or taxes-by-country report was found in the 20-F.
